gaps.sentence: We stopped at a cafe to ___ a chat.
gaps.explanation: have a chat is the fixed collocation for a friendly, informal conversation.

gaps.sentence: Students should ___ notes while they listen to the lecture.
gaps.explanation: take notes is the standard collocation for writing down information.

gaps.sentence: She ___ attention to every detail of the contract.
The scientists are ___ research into new forms of energy.
gaps.explanation: do research (into something) is the collocation; 'make research' is wrong.

gaps.sentence: Everyone agreed the suggestion was utterly ___.
gaps.explanation: utterly ridiculous is the standard collocation; 'utterly' is used with extreme adjectives.

gaps.sentence: Most children learn to ___ the time before they start school.
gaps.hint: fixed phrase: ___ the time (read a clock)
gaps.explanation: tell the time means to be able to read a clock; it is a fixed expression.

gaps.sentence: The two sides struggled to ___ an agreement before the deadline.
The ministry has ___ an inquiry into the collapse.
gaps.explanation: 'Order an inquiry' = officially commission a formal investigation.
